submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires retrospectively, on the token itself, when that token opens a syntactic or orthographic unit the model must then continue and is itself structural rather than a whole lexical word: a word-initial consonant fragment that leaves the word incomplete ('r' in 'ruminates', 'v' in 'check.v1', 'Br' in 'BranchId', 'ch' in 'chown', 'V' in 'VERSION'), a singular auxiliary or copula that starts a sentence after a completed one (Does 2.8, Is 2.6, Was 1.8, Has 1.5, Did 1.0) or heads a relative or coordinated clause ('which is', 'that is'), the clitic negation -n't, and a lexically specific set of light control verbs (makes, made, calls, called, tells, gives, helps, allows, lets). It stays at zero on the later pieces of the same word, on whole single-token words even when they open a sentence or clause ('version', 'chair', 'chimney', 'committee', ' The', ' A'), on non-singular and modal auxiliaries (Do 0.4, Are 0.5, Were 0.7, Can 0.3, Will 0.5), on copulas after a dummy or adjacent pronoun ('there is' 0.0, 'it is' 0.0), on finite verbs outside that light set (seems, appears, shows, sells, suggests, contains, produces, opens, uses, needs, puts, all 0.0), and on any text after the peak.

rival_explanations: The pole is a flat lexical detector that fires on a fixed list of token identities (is/does/makes/'t/also plus a set of short fragments) whatever the context, so it should fire as strongly on 'Do the machines' as on 'Does the machine', and on 'it is' and 'The report mentions chown' as on 'which is' and sentence-initial 'Is'.

The pole marks sustained formal, technical or code-boilerplate register, the qualification-marker family its layer-5 neighbour N867+ detects, so its activation should grow with the length and formality of the surrounding passage and stay near zero in short casual prose and plain description.

The pole fires on any token that opens a new word after whitespace (a space-prefixed piece or a line-initial tab) whenever more word material follows, so whole words such as 'version', 'committee', 'chimney' and 'machine' should fire as strongly as fragments when a word continues after them.

top_examples.text:
An equivalence algorithm to point out errors for basic LOTOS in a distributed system environment and its prototype

LOTOS formal description technique (FDT) is applied to the formal description of distributed systems and the specification of OSI protocol layers. LOTOS is difficult to understand and to learn because it is based on a mathematical model. In this paper, for supporting the knowledge acquisition of learners studying basic LOTOS, we suggest a new algorithm that can verify an equivalence relation, find an error location, and correct an error when the error occurs at another process. Finally, we give an example of a prototype program for an educational support system for basic LOTOS.

readings.explanation: The pole fires retrospectively, on the token itself, when that token opens a syntactic or orthographic unit the model must then continue and is itself structural rather than a whole lexical word: a word-initial consonant fragment that leaves the word incomplete ('r' in 'ruminates', 'v' in 'check.v1', 'Br' in 'BranchId', 'ch' in 'chown', 'V' in 'VERSION'), a singular auxiliary or copula that starts a sentence after a completed one (Does 2.8, Is 2.6, Was 1.8, Has 1.5, Did 1.0) or heads a relative or coordinated clause ('which is', 'that is'), the clitic negation -n't, and a lexically specific set of light control verbs (makes, made, calls, called, tells, gives, helps, allows, lets). It stays at zero on the later pieces of the same word, on whole single-token words even when they open a sentence or clause ('version', 'chair', 'chimney', 'committee', ' The', ' A'), on non-singular and modal auxiliaries (Do 0.4, Are 0.5, Were 0.7, Can 0.3, Will 0.5), on copulas after a dummy or adjacent pronoun ('there is' 0.0, 'it is' 0.0), on finite verbs outside that light set (seems, appears, shows, sells, suggests, contains, produces, opens, uses, needs, puts, all 0.0), and on any text after the peak.

The pole is a flat lexical detector that fires on a fixed list of token identities (is/does/makes/'t/also plus a set of short fragments) whatever the context, so it should fire as strongly on 'Do the machines' as on 'Does the machine', and on 'it is' and 'The report mentions chown' as on 'which is' and sentence-initial 'Is'.

The pole marks sustained formal, technical or code-boilerplate register, the qualification-marker family its layer-5 neighbour N867+ detects, so its activation should grow with the length and formality of the surrounding passage and stay near zero in short casual prose and plain description.

The pole fires on any token that opens a new word after whitespace (a space-prefixed piece or a line-initial tab) whenever more word material follows, so whole words such as 'version', 'committee', 'chimney' and 'machine' should fire as strongly as fragments when a word continues after them.

verdict.notes: hard_negative: 16/20 passed; positive_holdout: 9/10 passed; counterfactual: 9/9 passed; lookahead_consistency: 1/1 passed. All gates passed.
